questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the total solar eclipse of 12 August 2026:
1. It was the first total solar eclipse visible from mainland Europe since 1999.
2. Its path of totality crossed Greenland, Iceland and Spain.
3. In Spain, totality occurred around midday, with the Sun high in the sky.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The eclipse of 12 August 2026 was the first total solar eclipse visible from mainland Europe since 1999. Its totality path crossed Greenland, Iceland and Spain (including the Balearic Islands), touching a small part of Portugal. In Spain totality came in the evening, around 8:26-8:31 p.m. CEST, with the Sun low in the west.
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement 3 is wrong: in Spain totality came in the evening, just before sunset.

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the Senedd (Welsh Parliament) election of 7 May 2026:
1. The Senedd continued to have 60 members.
2. Plaid Cymru won the most seats, 43.
3. Labour lost its position as the largest party for the first time since devolution began in 1999.

solution.explanation: The 2026 Senedd election, held by closed-list proportional representation, filled an enlarged chamber of 96 members (up from 60). Plaid Cymru won 43 seats, Reform UK 34 and Labour 9; Labour lost government and its largest-party status for the first time since 1999. Plaid Cymru leader Rhun ap Iorwerth became First Minister.
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement 1 is wrong: the Senedd was enlarged from 60 to 96 members for this election.

C held his for 4 months, but it was also credited with ₹20,000 of local fees. Who can have the balance paid out to them at the time of departure under RBI's rules?

solution.explanation: A tourist's NRO balance may be paid at departure provided the account was maintained for not more than six months and was not credited with any local funds other than interest. A meets both conditions; B exceeds six months; C received local funds.
steps: Condition 2: no local credits except interest → A, B
solution.why_others_wrong: B fails the six-month condition; C fails the no-local-funds condition.

fact_checks.claim: The balance in the NRO account may be paid to the account holder at the time of his departure from India provided the account has been maintained for a period not exceeding six months and the account has not been credited with any local funds, other than interest accrued thereon

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: An exporter receives USD 50,000 of export proceeds in its EEFC account in March 2026 and, in April, uses USD 20,000 of these March accruals for an approved import payment; it has no forward commitments. Under RBI's Master Direction – Deposits and Accounts, how much of the March accruals must be converted into rupees, and by when?

options.text: Nothing, because EEFC balances never need conversion

solution.explanation: 100% of foreign exchange earnings can be credited to EEFC, but the total accruals of a calendar month must be converted into rupees on or before the last day of the succeeding calendar month, after adjusting for use for approved purposes or forward commitments. March accruals of 50,000 less 20,000 used leaves USD 30,000 to convert by 30 April 2026.
steps: Deadline: last day of the next month = 30 April 2026
solution.why_others_wrong: Conversion is net of approved use and due by the end of the following month, not the same month or a year later; balances are not exempt from conversion.
solution.final_answer: Option A: USD 30,000, on or before 30 April 2026

fact_checks.claim: Credits permitted: 100 percent of the foreign exchange earnings by way of inward remittance ...; the sum total of the accruals in the account during a calendar month should be converted into Rupees on or before the last day of the succeeding calendar month after adjusting for utilization of the balances for approved purposes or forward commitments

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Priya lives in Chennai, but the OVD she has shows her old New Delhi address. To open an account in Chennai she can offer: (P) an electricity bill dated six weeks ago, (Q) a post-paid mobile bill dated three months ago, (R) a municipal property tax receipt. Under RBI's KYC Directions, 2025 for commercial banks, which can serve as deemed OVDs for proof of address, and what must she do afterwards?

options.text: P and R; submit an OVD with her current address within three months
P, Q and R; no further document is needed
P and Q; submit an OVD with her current address within 30 days
R only; submit an OVD with her current address within one year

solution.explanation: If the OVD does not show the current address, a customer may give a deemed OVD such as a utility bill not more than two months old or a property/municipal tax receipt, but must submit an OVD with the current address within three months. The three-month-old mobile bill is too old.
steps: Utility bill ≤ 2 months → P valid, Q not
OVD with current address within 3 months
solution.why_others_wrong: Q is older than two months; the follow-up OVD is due within three months, not one year or 30 days, and it is required.
solution.final_answer: Option A: P and R; submit an OVD with her current address within three months

fact_checks.claim: when the customer furnishes an OVD that does not have an updated address, the bank shall deem ... utility bill which is not more than two months old of any service provider (electricity, telephone, post-paid mobile phone ...); property or Municipal tax receipt ... the customer shall submit OVD with current address within a period of three months of submitting the documents specified at (b) above

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness

options.text: Both accounts must be closed on his return and the money credited to a resident savings account
The NRE account may continue as an NRE account until he has stayed in India for 182 days
The NRE account must at once be redesignated as a resident account or moved to an RFC account, while the FCNR(B) deposit may continue till maturity at the contracted rate
The FCNR(B) deposit must be broken immediately, while the NRE account can continue till he chooses to close it

FCNR(B) deposits may continue till maturity at the contracted rate; on maturity they are converted into resident rupee or RFC accounts.
steps: NRE → redesignate as resident / transfer to RFC immediately

solution.final_answer: Option C: The NRE account must at once be redesignated as a resident account or moved to an RFC account, while the FCNR(B) deposit may continue till maturity at the contracted rate

The amalgamation of Oriental Bank of Commerce and United Bank of India into Punjab National Bank was a scheme framed by RBI under Section 45 of the Banking Regulation Act. II. The amalgamation of The Lakshmi Vilas Bank with DBS Bank India Ltd. came into force on 27 November 2020, from when LVB's branches functioned as DBS Bank India branches. III. Both these amalgamations were sanctioned under section 9 of the Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Acts. Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The OBC/UBI scheme was issued by the Government of India under section 9 of the Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Acts of 1970 and 1980, not by RBI. Being a private bank, LVB was outside the bank nationalisation Acts.

III: false (LVB was not a nationalised bank)
solution.why_others_wrong: Statements I and III are wrong, so every option containing them is wrong.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: In its data on transmission to lending rates, RBI reports an 'interest rate effect' on the weighted average lending rate (WALR) separately from the total change. How is the interest rate effect calculated?

options.text: By counting only loans to the government and public sector undertakings
By keeping the weights (loan composition) constant, as of January 2025
By deducting the change in the repo rate from the change in WALR
By excluding all loans linked to external benchmarks

solution.explanation: WALR can change because rates on each loan category change (interest rate effect) or because the mix of loans shifts (composition effect). RBI isolates the interest rate effect by holding the weights constant as of January 2025; e.g. in December 2025 the fresh-loan WALR fell 69 bps, but the interest rate effect was 78 bps.
steps: Total WALR change = interest rate effect + composition effect

questions.question_text: RBI reported the cumulative change since February 2025 in banks' rates as follows. Up to April 2026: WALR on fresh loans −83 bps, on outstanding loans −89 bps; WADTDR on fresh deposits −85 bps, on outstanding deposits −50 bps. Up to June 2026: WALR fresh −80, outstanding −91; WADTDR fresh −63, outstanding −51. What happened during May–June 2026?

options.text: Fresh deposit rates rose by about 22 bps, but fresh lending rates fell by about 3 bps
All four rates rose, led by outstanding deposit rates
Fresh deposit rates rose by about 22 bps and fresh lending rates by about 3 bps, while rates on outstanding loans eased by about 2 bps
Fresh lending rates fell by a further 3 bps and fresh deposit rates fell by 22 bps

solution.explanation: Change in May–June = (cumulative to June) − (cumulative to April). WALR fresh: −80 − (−83) = +3; WALR outstanding: −91 − (−89) = −2; WADTDR fresh: −63 − (−85) = +22; WADTDR outstanding: −51 − (−50) = −1. This matches the Governor's remark that transmission moderated with hardening of deposit and lending rates as credit demand stayed strong.
solution.why_others_wrong: Fresh lending rates rose, not fell; outstanding rates eased slightly, so not all four rose.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Fresh deposit rates rose by about 22 bps and fresh lending rates by about 3 bps, while rates on outstanding loans eased by about 2 bps

options.text: The auction was oversubscribed about 3.2 times and allotment was pro rata
About 31.6% was taken up, at 1 bp below the repo rate; interest payable to RBI was about ₹13.65 crore
About 68.4% of the notified amount was taken up; interest payable to RBI was about ₹47.4 crore
Only about 31.6% of the notified amount was taken up, at 1 bp above the repo rate; interest payable to RBI was about ₹13.65 crore

solution.explanation: Take-up = 23,680 ÷ 75,000 = 31.6%. In a VRR, banks borrow from RBI and bid rates at or above the repo rate; the cut-off of 5.26% is 1 bp above 5.25%. Interest = 23,680 × 5.26% × 4/365 ≈ ₹13.65 crore. Low take-up showed banks' borrowing need was well below what RBI offered.
solution.why_others_wrong: Bids were below the notified amount (not oversubscribed); 5.26% is above, not below, the repo rate; 68.4% is the untaken share.

questions.question_text: On 30 January 2026 (repo rate 5.25%), RBI held a long-tenor Variable Rate Repo auction with a notified amount of ₹25,000 crore. Bids of ₹95,062 crore were received; ₹25,004 crore was allotted at a cut-off rate of 5.34% and a weighted average rate of 5.40%, with 38.37% partial allotment of bids at the cut-off rate. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Bids were about 3.8 times the notified amount; successful bidders paid their own (higher) bid rates, averaging 6 bps above the cut-off and 15 bps above the repo rate, and bids at the cut-off got only part of what they sought
Bids were about 3.8 times the notified amount; successful bidders paid on average 6 bps below the cut-off rate
Bids were about 3.8 times the notified amount, and every successful bidder paid the uniform cut-off rate of 5.34%
The auction was undersubscribed, so all bids were accepted in full at the repo rate

solution.concept: Reading a variable rate repo auction result
solution.explanation: Cover = 95,062 ÷ 25,000 ≈ 3.8 times. In a VRR, banks borrow and bid rates; RBI accepts the highest bids down to the cut-off (5.34%), the lowest accepted rate. Because the weighted average rate (5.40%) exceeds the cut-off, allotments were priced at the bidders' own rates (multiple price), not one uniform rate: 5.40 − 5.34 = 6 bps above cut-off; 5.40 − 5.25 = 15 bps above repo. Bids exactly at the cut-off were scaled down (38.37% allotment) to keep the total near the notified amount. The heavy demand led RBI to hold a second 90-day VRR (notified ₹2,00,000 crore) the same day.
solution.why_others_wrong: A uniform price would make the weighted average equal the cut-off; the auction was oversubscribed; in a repo auction accepted bids are at or above the cut-off, so the average cannot be below it.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Bids were about 3.8 times the notified amount; successful bidders paid their own (higher) bid rates, averaging 6 bps above the cut-off and 15 bps above the repo rate, and bids at the cut-off got only part of what they sought

fact_checks.claim: For the first time since the adoption of flexible inflation targeting (FIT), average headline inflation for a quarter at 1.7 per cent in Q2:2025-26, breached the lower tolerance threshold (2 per cent) of the inflation target (4 per cent). It dipped further to a mere 0.3 per cent in October 2025

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the CPI with base 2024=100 released by MoSPI:
I. Its weights come from HCES 2023-24, while base-period prices were collected from January to December 2024.
II. Food and beverages still have the largest weight, although it fell to 36.75% from 45.86%.
III. E-commerce prices are collected from online markets in every district of the country.
Which is/are correct?

solution.explanation: I and II are stated in MoSPI's release. III is wrong: e-commerce prices were added as an extra market only in 12 large towns with population above 25 lakh; physical market collection remains the backbone.
steps: I true (weight vs price reference periods)
solution.why_others_wrong: 'II only' omits I; options with III are wrong.
solution.final_answer: Option C: I and II only

Share of Food & Beverages is declined in the new series, however, it continues to remain the largest component of the CPI basket (weights: CPI 2012 45.86%; CPI 2024 36.75)
