questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Failure to meet the inflation target means average CPI inflation below 2% (or above 6%) for any three consecutive quarters. RBI reported: Q2:2025-26 average 1.7% (the first quarter ever below 2%); monthly inflation of 0.3% (October), 0.7% (November) and 1.3% (December 2025); and 2.7% (January), 3.2% (February) and 3.4% (March 2026). Was there a failure?

options.text: Yes; Q1, Q2 and Q3 of 2025-26 all averaged below 2%
No; Q2 and Q3 averaged below 2% (Q3 about 0.8%), but Q4 averaged about 3.1%, so there were only two consecutive quarters
No; because the lower band applies only if inflation turns negative
Yes; Q2, Q3 and Q4 of 2025-26 all averaged below 2%

solution.concept: Failure criteria under the RBI Act
solution.explanation: Q3 average = (0.3 + 0.7 + 1.3) ÷ 3 ≈ 0.77%; Q4 = (2.7 + 3.2 + 3.4) ÷ 3 = 3.1%. Q1:2025-26 was above 2% (Q2 was the first breach ever). So only Q2 and Q3 were below 2% – two quarters, not three. The CPI series changed base from January 2026, but every reading of Q4 is above 2%.
solution.why_others_wrong: Q1 was not below 2%; Q4 was above 2%; the lower threshold is 2%, not zero.
solution.final_answer: Option B: No; Q2 and Q3 averaged below 2% (Q3 about 0.8%), but Q4 averaged about 3.1%, so there were only two consecutive quarters

fact_checks.claim: Failure ... (b) the average inflation is less than the lower tolerance level for any three consecutive quarters

For the first time since the adoption of flexible inflation targeting (FIT), average headline inflation for a quarter at 1.7 per cent in Q2:2025-26 ... breached the lower tolerance threshold ... It dipped further to a mere 0.3 per cent in October 2025
Headline CPI inflation remained low at 0.7 per cent in November and 1.3 per cent in December, 2025
headline inflation increased to 3.2 per cent in February 2026 from 2.7 per cent in January
Headline CPI inflation inched up to 3.4 per cent in March and 3.5 per cent in April 2026

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.subtopic: Instruments: T-bills, CP, CD, call money
questions.question_text: Which day count convention is followed in India's money market, including for Treasury Bills?

solution.explanation: RBI's G-sec FAQ states that the money market uses actual/365 (actual days in the numerator, 365 in the year), and T-bills follow it; the bond market uses 30/360.
solution.why_others_wrong: 30/360 is the Indian bond-market convention; actual/360 and actual/actual are used elsewhere.

fact_checks.claim: Money market: The day count convention followed is actual/365 ... Hence, in the case of T-Bills, which are essentially money market instruments, money market convention is followed

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.subtopic: Instruments: T-bills, CP, CD, call money
questions.question_text: In February 2026 the RBI Governor explained why rates on commercial papers (CPs) and certificates of deposit (CDs) tightened in January 2026. Which reasons did he give?

options.text: Moderation in surplus liquidity, excess supply from bunched CP/CD redemptions, and year-end seasonal effects
Large OMO sales by RBI and a cut in the WMA limit
A repo rate hike in January 2026 and higher CRR
A ban on mutual funds investing in CPs and CDs

solution.explanation: The Governor cited (i) moderation in surplus liquidity, (ii) excess supply from bunching of CP and CD redemptions in January and (iii) year-end seasonal effects. RBI was in fact injecting durable liquidity then through OMO purchases and swaps.
solution.why_others_wrong: There was no repo hike or CRR increase then; no such MF ban; RBI was buying, not selling, G-secs.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Moderation in surplus liquidity, excess supply from bunched CP/CD redemptions, and year-end seasonal effects

fact_checks.claim: Money market rates, especially for commercial papers (CPs) and certificates of deposit (CDs), tightened in January 2026 reflecting (i) moderation in surplus liquidity; (ii) excess supply from bunching of redemptions in CPs and CDs in January; and (iii) year-end seasonal effects

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.subtopic: Instruments: T-bills, CP, CD, call money
questions.question_text: The June 2026 Governor's statement gave average rates since the April policy (3-month T-bill 5.34%, 3-month CD 6.75%, 3-month CP 6.99%) and between the February and April policies (5.32%, 7.16% and 7.45%). Which statement is correct?

options.text: CD rates eased the most (about 46 bps), while CP rates eased 41 bps
CP rates rose about 46 bps as liquidity tightened
CP rates eased the most (about 46 bps), CD rates about 41 bps, while the T-bill rate rose 2 bps
All three rates eased, the T-bill rate by 2 bps

solution.explanation: CP: 6.99 − 7.45 = −46 bps; CD: 6.75 − 7.16 = −41 bps; T-bill: 5.34 − 5.32 = +2 bps. Private paper (CP, CD) eased markedly while the sovereign T-bill rate was almost flat.
solution.why_others_wrong: CD fell 41 (not 46); the T-bill rate rose; CP rates fell, not rose.
solution.final_answer: Option C: CP rates eased the most (about 46 bps), CD rates about 41 bps, while the T-bill rate rose 2 bps

fact_checks.claim: The rates on 3-month treasury bill, 3-month certificates of deposit and 3-month commercial paper averaged 5.34 per cent, 6.75 per cent and 6.99 per cent, respectively, since April policy as compared to 5.32 per cent, 7.16 per cent and 7.45 per cent, respectively, between February and April policy

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.subtopic: Instruments: T-bills, CP, CD, call money
questions.question_text: Under RBI's rules described in its G-sec FAQ, which entities may re-repo government securities (including SDLs and T-bills) that they acquired under reverse repo?

options.text: Scheduled commercial banks, primary dealers, and mutual funds and insurance companies (with their regulators' approval) holding SGL accounts with RBI
Only RBI, as part of the LAF
Any individual investor holding a gilt account
Only scheduled commercial banks, and only overnight

solution.concept: Repo and re-repo in the money market
solution.explanation: A repo is borrowing by selling securities with an agreement to repurchase; a reverse repo is the lending side. Re-repo lets the lender use securities received in a reverse repo for its own repo. SCBs, PDs, and MFs and insurers (subject to their regulators' approval) maintaining SGL accounts with RBI may re-repo G-secs, including SDLs and T-bills.
steps: Reverse repo: lend cash, receive securities
Eligible: SCBs, PDs, MFs, insurers with SGL accounts
solution.why_others_wrong: Re-repo is a market facility, not an RBI-only one; it is not restricted to SCBs; individuals are not eligible.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Scheduled commercial banks, primary dealers, and mutual funds and insurance companies (with their regulators' approval) holding SGL accounts with RBI

fact_checks.claim: Scheduled commercial banks, Primary Dealers along with Mutual Funds and Insurance Companies (subject to the approval of the regulators concerned) maintaining Subsidiary General Ledger account with RBI are permitted to re-repo the government securities, including SDLs and Treasury Bills, acquired under reverse repo

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.subtopic: Instruments: T-bills, CP, CD, call money
questions.question_text: In December 2025 the Governor reported how money market rates had responded to the cumulative 100 bps repo cut of the easing cycle (up to 3 December 2025): WACR −110 bps, 3-month T-bill −113 bps, 3-month NBFC CP −124 bps and 3-month CD −140 bps. What does this show?

options.text: CP rates fell the most, while CD rates fell less than the repo cut
Only the call rate fell by more than the repo cut
Transmission was weak: no money market rate fell as much as the repo rate
Transmission to the money market was more than full: every rate fell by more than the repo cut, CDs the most

solution.explanation: All four rates fell by more than 100 bps (comfortable liquidity added to the rate cuts); the 3-month CD rate fell the most (140 bps).
solution.why_others_wrong: All rates fell more than 100 bps, so the 'weak' and 'only the call rate' options are wrong; CD (not CP) fell the most.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Transmission to the money market was more than full: every rate fell by more than the repo cut, CDs the most

fact_checks.claim: In response to the cumulative policy repo rate cut of 100 bps in the current easing cycle (up to December 03), the WACR, the 3-month T-bill rate, the rate on 3-month CPs issued by NBFCs, and the 3-month CD rate declined by 110 bps, 113 bps, 124 bps, and 140 bps, respectively

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.subtopic: Instruments: T-bills, CP, CD, call money
questions.question_text: The February 2026 Governor's statement said that, after the cumulative 125 bps repo cut, the 3-month T-bill, 3-month NBFC CP and 3-month CD rates had fallen by 119, 143 and 127 bps up to end-December 2025, but then hardened by 6, 73 and 84 bps respectively between 1 January and 4 February 2026. What was the net decline in each by 4 February 2026?

options.text: T-bill 113 bps, CP 70 bps, CD 43 bps – only the CD rate below the repo cut
T-bill 106 bps, CP 57 bps, CD 41 bps – all below the repo cut
T-bill 113 bps, CP 70 bps, CD 43 bps – all now below the 125 bps repo cut
T-bill 125 bps, CP 216 bps, CD 211 bps

solution.explanation: Net decline = earlier fall − later rise: T-bill 119 − 6 = 113; CP 143 − 73 = 70; CD 127 − 84 = 43. All three are now below 125 bps, though before January the CP and CD rates had fallen by more than the repo cut.
solution.why_others_wrong: Adding the rises double-counts; the T-bill and CP declines are also below 125; the last option miscalculates.
solution.final_answer: Option C: T-bill 113 bps, CP 70 bps, CD 43 bps – all now below the 125 bps repo cut

fact_checks.claim: the WACR, the 3-month T-bill rate, the 3-month CP issued by NBFCs, and the 3-month CD rate declined by 89 bps, 119 bps, 143 bps, and 127 bps, respectively up to end-December, 2025. However, since the beginning of January and up to February 4, 2026, the 3-month T-bill rate, the 3-month CP issued by NBFCs, and the 3-month CD rate have hardened by 6 bps, 73 bps and 84 bps, respectively

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: RBI's amendment directions of 7 October 2026 revise the methodology for minimum capital requirements for counterparty credit risk from 1 April 2027. To which commercial banks do they apply mandatorily?

options.text: Only foreign banks operating in India through branches
All commercial banks, including small finance banks and payments banks
Banks with an international presence or with derivatives outstanding (book value) of ₹25,000 crore and above
Only the Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs)

solution.concept: Scope of the revised counterparty credit risk framework
solution.explanation: The Commercial Banks – Forthcoming Instructions Amendment Directions, 2026 (7 October 2026), effective 1 April 2027, apply to commercial banks with an international presence or with book value of derivatives outstanding of ₹25,000 crore and above on a consolidated group-wide basis. The remaining commercial banks may choose either the Current Exposure Method (CEM) or the Standardised Approach for Counterparty Credit Risk (SA-CCR).
steps: Mandatory: international presence, or derivatives book ≥ ₹25,000 crore
solution.why_others_wrong: The scope is not defined by D-SIB status or by foreign ownership, and other banks are given a choice rather than being covered mandatorily.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Banks with an international presence or with derivatives outstanding (book value) of ₹25,000 crore and above

fact_checks.claim: These Amendment Directions shall come into effect from April 1, 2027; shall be applicable to commercial banks with an international presence or with book value of derivative outstanding of ₹ 25,000 crore and above as on the reporting date, on a consolidated group wide basis. However, remaining commercial banks may choose to adopt either the Current Exposure Method (CEM) or the Standardised Approach for Counterparty Credit Risk (SA-CCR)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: RBI's circular of 23 September 2026 notified a Government of India-supported Line of Credit extended by Exim Bank to which country, for ₹4,850 crore?

solution.explanation: Exim Bank's ₹4,850 crore GOI-supported LoC to the Government of the Republic of Maldives finances development projects; at least 75% of the contract value must be supplied from India. The agreement is effective from 27 August 2026.
solution.why_others_wrong: The circular concerns only the Maldives.

fact_checks.claim: Exim Bank's GOI-supported Line of Credit (LOC) for ₹ 4,850 crores the Government of Maldives, for financing various developmental projects in Maldives ... goods, works and services of the value of at least 75% of the contract price ... shall be supplied by the Seller from India

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: By a circular of 1 October 2026 on online submission of Form A2 for outward remittances, what did RBI change for Authorised Dealers' internal guidelines?

options.text: They can be framed only for remittances up to USD 25,000 a year
They must now be approved by RBI before use
They now need approval of the Foreign Exchange Dealers' Association of India
They may be approved by the Board or by a Board Committee/Management Committee to which the Board has delegated powers

solution.explanation: Earlier (July 2024 circular) ADs had to frame internal guidelines for Form A2-based remittances with Board approval. The October 2026 circular allows approval by the Board or any Board Committee or Management Committee with delegated powers; other instructions remain unchanged.
solution.why_others_wrong: No RBI pre-approval or FEDAI approval is required; the circular adds no amount ceiling.
solution.final_answer: Option D: They may be approved by the Board or by a Board Committee/Management Committee to which the Board has delegated powers

fact_checks.claim: Authorised Dealers shall frame appropriate internal guidelines with the approval of their Board or any Board Committee / Management Committee to which powers have been delegated by the Board

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's amendment of 22 September 2026 to the commercial banks' investment portfolio directions, how must a bank value units of an unlisted InvIT or REIT that fails to compute and disclose its NAV as required by SEBI?

options.text: At the last traded price on any exchange

solution.explanation: Unquoted InvIT and REIT units are valued at the NAV the trust discloses. If the trust fails to compute and disclose NAV in the manner and frequency SEBI specifies, or the units are infrequently traded, they are valued at ₹1 – a conservative rule.
solution.why_others_wrong: Face value, last traded price and cost-based haircuts are not the prescribed treatment.

fact_checks.claim: Units: The valuation shall be done at the NAV as disclosed by the InvIT. Where an InvIT fails to compute and disclose the NAV in the manner and frequency specified under SEBI (Infrastructure Investment Trusts) Regulations, 2014, the value of its units shall be treated as ₹1

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
RBI's amendment directions of 1 October 2026 on acquisition of shares in banks introduced a one-time approval for 'qualifying persons'. Consider:
I. Qualifying persons are SEBI-registered mutual funds, PFRDA-registered pension funds and IRDAI-registered insurers that do not belong to the bank's promoter group or group.
II. The one-time approval covers subsequent acquisitions of major shareholding up to 10% of the bank's paid-up capital or voting rights, on an aggregate basis.
III. With the one-time approval, prior approval is no longer needed even for the initial acquisition of major shareholding.
Which is/are correct?

solution.explanation: I and II follow the amendment's definitions and proviso. III is wrong: RBI said prior approval stays mandatory for the initial acquisition of major shareholding; the relief is only for subsequent acquisitions after a holding has fallen below 5%. Applications go through PRAVAAH.
steps: III: initial acquisition still needs prior approval
solution.why_others_wrong: 'II only' omits I; options with III are wrong.
solution.final_answer: Option D: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: While obtaining prior approval shall continue to be mandatory for initial acquisition of major shareholding in a banking company ... decided to grant one-time approval for subsequent acquisitions of major shareholding in the same banking company by mutual funds, insurance companies and pension funds

'qualifying person' ... is a mutual fund registered with the Securities and Exchange Board of India, or a pension fund registered with the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority, or an insurance company registered with the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India; and ... does not belong to the promoter group or group of the investee banking company ... one-time approval ... for subsequent acquisitions of major shareholding up to 10 per cent of the paid-up share capital or voting rights

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's income recognition and asset classification norms, advances against certain instruments need not be treated as NPAs if adequate margin is available. Advances against which of the following are NOT covered by this exemption?

solution.explanation: RBI's IRAC Directions, 2025 exempt advances against term deposits, NSCs eligible for surrender, KVPs and life insurance policies from NPA treatment as long as adequate margin is available. Advances against gold ornaments, government securities and all other securities are expressly not covered.
steps: Exempt (with adequate margin): term deposits, NSCs, KVPs, life insurance policies
Not exempt: gold ornaments, government securities, other securities
solution.why_others_wrong: Term deposits, KVPs and life insurance policies are all in the exempted list.

fact_checks.claim: Advances against term deposits, NSCs eligible for surrender, KVPs and life insurance policies need not be treated as NPAs, provided adequate margin is available; advances against gold ornaments, government securities and all other securities are not covered by this exemption

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI), the regulator that implements the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, was established on:

solution.explanation: IBBI was established on 1 October 2016 under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016. It is a key pillar of the ecosystem that implements the Code (it marks 1 October as its Annual Day).
steps: IBBI established under the Code on 1 October 2016
solution.why_others_wrong: The other dates are not IBBI's establishment date.

fact_checks.claim: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India was established on 1st October, 2016 under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Asset reconstruction companies (ARCs) registered under the SARFAESI Act acquire stressed loans and issue security receipts (SRs). According to RBI's FAQs on ARCs, what is the maximum realisation period for financial assets acquired by an ARC?

options.text: Five years from the date of acquisition
Eight years from the date of acquisition
Ten years from the date of acquisition
Three years from the date of acquisition

solution.explanation: RBI's ARC FAQs (September 2026) refer to the maximum realisation period of 8 years from the date of acquisition. A transferee ARC cannot issue SRs to other qualified buyers for such assets after the eight-year period from the first acquisition has expired.
steps: ARC acquires asset and issues SRs
solution.why_others_wrong: Three, five and ten years are not the prescribed window.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Eight years from the date of acquisition

fact_checks.claim: ARCs are not prohibited from transferring financial assets to another ARC even after completion of the maximum realisation period of 8 years from the date of acquisition, but the transferee ARC shall not issue SRs to other QBs after the expiry of the stipulated eight-year period

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A bank's loan is backed by a guarantee of the Central Government. Interest has been overdue for more than 90 days. Under RBI's IRAC Directions, 2025, when will this account be treated as an NPA?

options.text: Only when the Government repudiates its guarantee when invoked
Never, since sovereign-guaranteed loans are always standard
Only after it remains overdue for 12 months
Immediately, since interest is overdue for more than 90 days

solution.explanation: Credit facilities backed by a Central Government guarantee, though overdue, are treated as NPA only when the Government repudiates its guarantee when invoked. This exemption is not for income recognition. State Government guaranteed advances, by contrast, follow the normal 90-day norm.
steps: Central Government guarantee → NPA only on repudiation when invoked
State Government guarantee → normal 90-day overdue norm
solution.why_others_wrong: The 90-day norm applies to State (not Central) Government guaranteed advances; there is no 12-month rule; the account is not standard for ever, as repudiation makes it an NPA.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Only when the Government repudiates its guarantee when invoked

fact_checks.claim: The credit facilities backed by guarantee of the Central Government though overdue shall be treated as NPA only when the Government repudiates its guarantee when invoked; State Government guaranteed advances attract the norms if dues remain overdue for more than 90 days

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: When a fraud is detected in a borrower account, a bank must normally provide for the entire amount due immediately. To smooth the impact on quarterly profits, over what maximum period may it spread this provision?

options.text: Eight quarters from the date of the fraud
Two quarters after the fraud is reported
Until the end of the next financial year
Four quarters, starting with the quarter in which the fraud is detected

solution.explanation: Under the IRAC Directions, a bank has the option to make the fraud provision over a period not exceeding four quarters, commencing with the quarter of detection. If this spills into the next financial year, the unprovided amount at year-end is debited to 'other reserves'.
steps: Option: spread over up to four quarters from the quarter of detection
solution.why_others_wrong: Two quarters is too short; eight quarters and 'end of next year' exceed the four-quarter limit.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Four quarters, starting with the quarter in which the fraud is detected

fact_checks.claim: A bank shall normally provide for the entire amount due immediately upon a fraud being detected; it has the option to make the provisions over a period not exceeding four quarters, commencing from the quarter in which the fraud has been detected

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: What provision must a bank hold on its standard-account exposure to a company that has a director (other than a nominee director of a government or financial institution brought in at the time of distress) whose name appears more than once in the list of wilful defaulters?

solution.explanation: The IRAC Directions prescribe a provision of 5% on existing loans or exposures to companies with such director(s), even when the accounts are standard, well above the normal standard-asset rate.
steps: Director appears more than once in wilful defaulter list
solution.why_others_wrong: 0.40% is the general standard-asset rate; 1% applies to commercial real estate; 15% is the substandard rate.

fact_checks.claim: The provisioning in respect of existing loans / exposures to companies having director(s) (other than nominee directors of government / financial institutions brought on board at the time of distress), whose name(s) appear more than once in the list of wilful defaulters, shall be five per cent in cases of standard accounts

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's FAQs on asset reconstruction companies (September 2026), can an ARC restructure a borrower account that the lender has classified as fraud or wilful defaulter?

options.text: No, and the ARC must sell such accounts within one year
No, unless the existing promoters are replaced and the company is totally delinked from them
Yes, but only by converting debt into equity
Yes, if the restructuring is approved by the ARC's Board

solution.explanation: ARCs are not permitted to restructure accounts classified as fraud or wilful defaulter. Restructuring includes rescheduling, conversion of debt into equity and additional funding. The exception: where the existing promoters are replaced by new promoters and the borrower company is totally delinked from the erstwhile promoters/management, the ARC may consider restructuring based on viability.
steps: Fraud / wilful defaulter accounts → no restructuring by ARC
Exception: promoters replaced and company delinked from them
solution.why_others_wrong: Board approval does not override the bar; debt-equity conversion is itself a form of restructuring; there is no one-year sale rule.
solution.final_answer: Option B: No, unless the existing promoters are replaced and the company is totally delinked from them

fact_checks.claim: ARCs are not permitted to restructure borrower accounts classified as fraud/ wilful defaulter; however, where the existing promoters are replaced by new promoters and the borrower company is totally delinked from such erstwhile promoters/management, ARCs may take a view on restructuring based on viability

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Under RBI's IRAC Directions, 2025, certain agricultural loans follow the crop-season norms for NPA classification instead of the 90-day norm. Which of the following loans qualify for the crop-season norms?
P. ₹50 lakh to an individual farmer against pledge of his produce for 10 months
Q. ₹75 lakh to an individual farmer against pledge of his produce for 6 months
R. ₹2 crore to a farmer producer organisation (aggregate borrowing ₹3 crore) against pledge of produce for 9 months
S. ₹2 crore to a corporate farmer against pledge of produce for 15 months

solution.concept: Agricultural loans and crop-season NPA norms
solution.explanation: Crop-season norms apply to pledge loans to individual farmers up to ₹60 lakh for not more than 12 months, and to corporate farmers, FPOs, partnership firms and co-operatives of farmers (aggregate limit ₹4 crore per borrower) for pledge loans up to ₹2.5 crore for not more than 12 months. Other agricultural loans follow the 90-day norm.
steps: R: aggregate ₹3 crore ≤ ₹4 crore; ₹2 crore ≤ ₹2.5 crore; 9 months → qualifies
solution.why_others_wrong: Q exceeds the ₹60 lakh cap for individuals; S exceeds the 12-month period.
solution.final_answer: Option C: P and R only

fact_checks.claim: Crop-season norms apply to loans to individual farmers up to ₹60 lakh against pledge / hypothecation of agricultural produce for a period not exceeding twelve months, and to loans to corporate farmers, FPOs, partnership firms and co-operatives of farmers up to an aggregate limit of ₹4 crore per borrower, including loans up to ₹2.5 crore against pledge of produce for not more than twelve months; other agricultural loans follow the 90 days delinquency norm

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The first paper issued by the Basel Committee, in 1975, came to be known as the 'Concordat'. What did it deal with?

options.text: Capital requirements for market risk using internal models
A minimum capital ratio of 8% of risk-weighted assets
Sharing supervisory responsibility for banks' foreign establishments between host and home supervisors
Liquidity standards to survive a 30-day stress period

solution.explanation: The 1975 Concordat set out principles for sharing supervisory responsibility for banks' foreign branches, subsidiaries and joint ventures between host and parent (home) supervisors, to close gaps in international supervisory coverage. It was revised in May 1983.
steps: 1975 Concordat → home/host supervision of foreign establishments
solution.why_others_wrong: The other options describe later Basel standards.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Sharing supervisory responsibility for banks' foreign establishments between host and home supervisors

fact_checks.claim: The 1975 paper known as the Concordat set out principles for sharing supervisory responsibility for banks' foreign branches, subsidiaries and joint ventures between host and parent (or home) supervisory authorities

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The Basel Committee's 'Core Principles for Effective Banking Supervision', first published in September 1997 with 25 principles, now contain how many principles after the latest revision in April 2024?

solution.explanation: The Core Principles began with 25 basic principles in 1997. After several revisions, most recently in April 2024, the document now includes 29 principles.
solution.why_others_wrong: 25 was the original number; 24 (the CPMI-IOSCO PFMIs) and 30 are distractors.

fact_checks.claim: When first published in September 1997, the paper set out 25 basic principles; after several revisions, most recently in April 2024, the document now includes 29 principles

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Basel III introduced two liquidity standards. The Liquidity Coverage Ratio covers funding needs over a 30-day stress period. What is the Net Stable Funding Ratio (NSFR) intended to address?

options.text: Concentration of large exposures to one counterparty
Maturity mismatches over the entire balance sheet
Intraday liquidity needs in payment systems

solution.explanation: In the Basel Committee's description, the LCR is meant to provide enough cash for a 30-day stress period, while the NSFR is a longer-term ratio intended to address maturity mismatches over the entire balance sheet.
steps: NSFR: longer term, maturity mismatch across the balance sheet
solution.why_others_wrong: Intraday liquidity, large exposures and operational risk are covered by other standards.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Maturity mismatches over the entire balance sheet

fact_checks.claim: Basel III liquidity requirements: the Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR), intended to provide enough cash to cover funding needs over a 30-day period of stress; and a longer-term ratio, the Net Stable Funding Ratio (NSFR), intended to address maturity mismatches over the entire balance sheet

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Which Basel III requirement sets a minimum amount of loss-absorbing capital relative to all of a bank's assets and off-balance sheet exposures, regardless of risk weighting?

solution.concept: Leverage ratio as a non-risk-based measure
solution.explanation: The Basel III leverage ratio is a simple, non-risk-based backstop: capital relative to total exposures, irrespective of risk weights. The buffers are add-ons to risk-based capital, and the LCR is a liquidity measure.
solution.why_others_wrong: The two buffers are percentages of risk-weighted assets; the LCR concerns liquid assets, not capital.

fact_checks.claim: Basel III includes a leverage ratio - a minimum amount of loss-absorbing capital relative to all of a bank's assets and off-balance sheet exposures regardless of risk weighting

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The Basel Committee completed its Basel III post-crisis reforms in 2017. Which element of these reforms limits the extent to which banks can use internal models to reduce their risk-based capital requirements?

options.text: The output floor, based on the revised standardised approaches

solution.explanation: The 2017 reforms revised the standardised approaches for credit, CVA and operational risk and added a revised leverage ratio, a leverage ratio buffer for G-SIBs and an output floor. The output floor is based on the revised standardised approaches and limits how far internal models can reduce RWAs, to cut excessive variability in risk-weighted assets.
steps: Purpose: curb RWA variability from internal models
solution.why_others_wrong: The conservation buffer restricts payouts; Pillar 3 is disclosure; the NSFR is a funding ratio.
solution.final_answer: Option B: The output floor, based on the revised standardised approaches

fact_checks.claim: The final reforms also include a revised leverage ratio, a leverage ratio buffer for global systemically important banks and an output floor, based on the revised standardised approaches, which limits the extent to which banks can use internal models to reduce risk-based capital requirements

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A customer's non-callable fixed deposit, normally excluded from a bank's LCR computation, is pledged as collateral for a loan to the customer. Under RBI's LCR amendments effective 1 April 2026, how is this deposit treated?

options.text: It stays excluded, as it is contractually non-callable
As a deduction from the bank's CET1 capital
As Level 1 high-quality liquid assets of the bank
As a callable deposit for LCR purposes

solution.explanation: RBI's April 2025 circular (effective 1 April 2026) says that a deposit hitherto excluded from LCR computation, such as a non-callable FD, that is contractually pledged as collateral for a credit facility shall be treated as callable for LCR purposes, so it attracts the relevant run-off.
steps: Pledged against a loan → treated as callable for LCR
solution.why_others_wrong: It does not stay excluded; a customer deposit is a liability, not the bank's HQLA; it has nothing to do with CET1 deductions.
solution.final_answer: Option D: As a callable deposit for LCR purposes

fact_checks.claim: In case a deposit, hitherto excluded from LCR computation (for instance, a non-callable fixed deposit), is contractually pledged as collateral to secure a credit facility or loan, such deposit shall be treated as callable for LCR purposes; these amendments come into force from April 01, 2026

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A bank has HQLA of ₹1,350 crore and total net cash outflows of ₹1,500 crore over the next 30 days, computed under the earlier rules. These outflows include ₹400 crore of deposits from educational trusts and partnership firms (not small business customers), which ran off at 100%. Under RBI's LCR amendments effective 1 April 2026, such funding is treated as from non-financial corporates. Assuming nothing else changes, how does the bank's LCR move?

options.text: From 90% to about 107.1%, crossing the 100% minimum
From 90% to 100%, just meeting the minimum
It stays at 90%, as only retail deposits were affected
From 90% to about 95.1%, still below the minimum

solution.concept: LCR = HQLA ÷ total net cash outflows over 30 days
solution.explanation: Funding from trusts, AoPs, partnerships, LLPs etc. (not treated as SBCs) now attracts a 40% run-off instead of 100%. Outflow on ₹400 crore falls from ₹400 crore to ₹160 crore, so net outflows fall to ₹1,260 crore.
steps: New outflow on trust deposits = 40% × 400 = ₹160 crore
solution.why_others_wrong: 100% ignores the reduced outflow's full effect; 95.1% would apply a smaller cut; the change applies to trusts and partnerships, not only retail deposits.
solution.final_answer: Option A: From 90% to about 107.1%, crossing the 100% minimum

fact_checks.claim: Funding from non-financial entities such as trusts (educational/religious/charitable), AoPs, partnerships, proprietorships, LLPs and other incorporated entities shall be categorised as funding from 'non-financial corporates' and attract a run-off rate of 40 per cent (as against 100 per cent currently prescribed), unless treated as SBCs; effective April 01, 2026

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the evolution of the Basel framework, as described by the Basel Committee:
I. The 1988 Accord's minimum capital ratio was to be implemented by the end of 1992.
II. The Market Risk Amendment of 1996 introduced the leverage ratio for the first time.
III. Basel III added a capital conservation buffer that, when breached, restricts payouts, with most reforms phased in between 2013 and 2019.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The 1988 Accord called for an 8% minimum to be implemented by end-1992 (I correct). The 1996 amendment added capital for market risk and allowed internal VaR models; the leverage ratio came only with Basel III (II wrong). Basel III added the capital conservation buffer, which restricts payouts when breached, with most reforms phased in between 2013 and 2019 (III correct).
steps: II ✗ (leverage ratio is a Basel III element)
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option including II is wrong.
solution.final_answer: Option B: I and III only

fact_checks.claim: The 1988 Accord called for a minimum ratio of capital to risk-weighted assets of 8% to be implemented by the end of 1992

The Market Risk Amendment (January 1996) incorporated a capital requirement for market risks; Basel III adds a capital conservation buffer that, when breached, restricts payouts, and a leverage ratio; most of the reforms are being phased in between 2013 and 2019

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: When a bank trades Priority Sector Lending Certificates (PSLCs) on RBI's e-Kuber portal, how is the counterparty decided?

options.text: Buyer and seller negotiate bilaterally and report the deal to RBI
Orders are matched anonymously by the portal; the bank cannot select the counterparty
NABARD allots a seller to each buyer
The buying bank selects the seller from a list of offers

solution.explanation: RBI's PSL FAQs state that order matching on the e-Kuber PSLC module is anonymous; neither buyer nor seller can select the counterparty. Partial matching can happen depending on premium and lots available. No transaction fee is charged for using the module.
steps: Anonymous order matching; no counterparty selection
solution.why_others_wrong: Buyers cannot pick sellers; NABARD has no allotment role; PSLCs are not bilateral OTC deals.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Orders are matched anonymously by the portal; the bank cannot select the counterparty

fact_checks.claim: The order matching will be done on anonymous basis through the portal and the buyer/seller cannot select the counterparty; partial matching will happen depending on the matching of premium and availability of category-wise PSLC lots

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Bank X sold a PSLC to Bank Y. Later, an RBI inspection finds that the loans underlying the PSLC were not eligible for priority sector classification. According to RBI's FAQs, whose achievement is reduced?

options.text: Only the buyer's (Bank Y), as it used the certificate
Neither bank's, since the PSLC has expired on 31 March
Only the seller's (Bank X); the buyer bears no risk

solution.explanation: RBI's FAQs say misclassifications, if any, are reduced from the achievement of the PSLC seller bank only. There is no risk for the PSLC buyer even if the underlying asset is later found ineligible.
steps: PSLC sold by X, bought by Y
Underlying declassified → X's achievement reduced; Y unaffected
solution.why_others_wrong: The buyer is protected; the loss is not shared; expiry does not erase the seller's misclassification.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Only the seller's (Bank X); the buyer bears no risk

fact_checks.claim: The misclassifications, if any, will have to be reduced from the achievement of PSLC seller bank only. There will be no risk for the PSLC buyer, even if the underlying asset of the traded PSLC gets misclassified

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A bank that missed its priority sector targets has outstanding shortfall deposits with NABARD, SIDBI and NHB. According to RBI's PSL FAQs, how are these deposits treated?

options.text: Only NABARD deposits count, and only towards the agriculture sub-target
NABARD deposits count under agriculture, SIDBI under MSME and NHB under housing; all count towards the overall target and are added to net bank credit for ANBC
They are deducted from net bank credit while computing ANBC
They count only towards the overall PSL target, not any sub-target, and are excluded from ANBC

solution.explanation: Outstanding deposits with NABARD on account of PSL shortfall count towards the agriculture sub-target; those with SIDBI and MUDRA under MSME lending; those with NHB under housing. All count for the overall PSL target and are added to net bank credit (NBC) in computing ANBC.
steps: All → overall target; added to NBC
solution.why_others_wrong: They do count towards sub-targets, are added to (not deducted from) NBC, and are not limited to NABARD.
solution.final_answer: Option B: NABARD deposits count under agriculture, SIDBI under MSME and NHB under housing; all count towards the overall target and are added to net bank credit for ANBC

fact_checks.claim: Outstanding deposits with NABARD on account of PSL shortfall are eligible to be reckoned towards Agriculture sub-target and overall PSL target; deposits with SIDBI and MUDRA under MSME lending; deposits with NHB under Housing; all outstanding deposits shall be added to Net Bank Credit for the computation of ANBC

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Bank loans for 'Agriculture Infrastructure' and for 'Food and Agro-processing' qualify as priority sector subject to an aggregate sanctioned limit per borrower from the banking system. What is that limit, and what happens if a borrower's aggregate exposure across banks exceeds it?

options.text: ₹100 crore; only the excess over ₹100 crore loses PSL status
₹100 crore; the entire exposure ceases to be priority sector
₹50 crore; only the excess over ₹50 crore loses PSL status
₹50 crore; the entire exposure ceases to be priority sector

solution.concept: Credit caps in agriculture PSL categories
solution.explanation: Each of these categories is subject to an aggregate sanctioned limit of ₹100 crore per borrower from the banking system. If the aggregate exposure across the banking industry exceeds ₹100 crore, the total exposure ceases to be classified as PSL, not merely the excess.
steps: Limit: ₹100 crore per borrower across banks
Breach → whole exposure loses PSL status
solution.why_others_wrong: The limit is ₹100 crore, not ₹50 crore, and the whole exposure (not just the excess) is affected.
solution.final_answer: Option B: ₹100 crore; the entire exposure ceases to be priority sector

fact_checks.claim: Loans for Agriculture Infrastructure or for Food & Agro-processing activity are each subject to an aggregate sanctioned limit of ₹100 crore per borrower from the banking system; if aggregate exposure across the banking industry exceeds ₹100 crore, total exposure will cease to be classified under PSL

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A farmer takes a crop loan from a bank against the pledge of gold jewellery. The loan is sanctioned on the basis of the scale of finance for the crop. Can it be classified under priority sector (agriculture)?

options.text: No; loans against gold are never eligible for priority sector
Yes; PSL is activity- and beneficiary-specific, so gold collateral alone does not make it ineligible
Yes, but only if the loan is below ₹2 lakh
No, unless the farmer also mortgages agricultural land

solution.concept: PSL is based on activity, not collateral
solution.explanation: RBI's FAQs say PSL guidelines are activity- and beneficiary-specific and not based on the type of collateral, so an agricultural loan does not become ineligible only because the security is gold jewellery. The bank should have assessed the credit requirement (scale of finance) for the activity.
steps: Test the purpose and borrower, not the collateral
solution.why_others_wrong: There is no blanket bar on gold-backed loans; ₹2 lakh is the limit for waiving collateral, not an eligibility cap; a land mortgage is not required.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Yes; PSL is activity- and beneficiary-specific, so gold collateral alone does not make it ineligible

fact_checks.claim: The PSL guidelines are activity and beneficiary specific and are not based on type of collateral; therefore, bank loans given for undertaking agriculture activities do not automatically become ineligible for priority sector classification only on account of the fact that underlying asset is gold jewellery/ornament

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A bank lends for farming to a partnership firm, one of whose partners holds 1.5 hectares of agricultural land. Can the loan be tagged under the Small and Marginal Farmers (SMF) category of PSL?

options.text: Yes, if the firm also qualifies as a micro enterprise
Yes, since the partner holds less than 2 hectares
No; loans to partnership firms are not eligible for the SMF category on the basis of a partner's land holding
Yes, but only for the partner's share of the loan

solution.explanation: SMF covers individuals, SHGs, JLGs, Farmer Producer Companies and co-operatives of farmers meeting the membership and land-holding criteria. RBI's FAQs say loans to partnership firms, co-borrowers or a company whose director holds up to 2 hectares are not eligible for the SMF category.
steps: SMF: individuals, SHGs, JLGs, FPCs, co-operatives of farmers
solution.why_others_wrong: A partner's holding does not make the firm an SMF; there is no pro-rata tagging; MSME status is irrelevant to the SMF tag.
solution.final_answer: Option C: No; loans to partnership firms are not eligible for the SMF category on the basis of a partner's land holding

fact_checks.claim: Loans to partnership firms/co-borrowers or any director of a company holding agriculture land upto 2 hectares are not eligible to be classified under the SMF category of PSL

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A domestic commercial bank has net bank credit (NBC) of ₹50,000 crore. During the year it bought PSLCs of ₹3,000 crore and sold PSLCs of ₹1,000 crore (all outstanding), and it has ₹1,500 crore of outstanding PSL-shortfall deposits with NABARD. Assume no other ANBC adjustments and that CEOBSE is lower. What is its overall PSL target (40% of ANBC)?

solution.concept: ANBC adjustments for PSLCs and shortfall deposits
solution.explanation: RBI's FAQs say the net PSLC position (buy minus sell) is added to NBC, and outstanding shortfall deposits with NABARD/SIDBI/MUDRA/NHB are also added to NBC, in computing ANBC.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹20,000 crore ignores both adjustments; ₹20,800 crore ignores the deposits; ₹21,800 crore adds gross PSLC purchases instead of the net position.

fact_checks.claim: The net PSLC outstanding (PSLC Buy minus PSLC Sell) is added to the Net Bank Credit; the effect of PSLC buy is increase in ANBC and of PSLC sell is decrease in ANBC
All outstanding deposits with NABARD, SIDBI, MUDRA and NHB on account of PSL shortfall shall be added to Net Bank Credit (NBC) for the computation of ANBC

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under the Reserve Bank – Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2026, to which e-mail address should a complaint be sent if it is not filed on the CMS portal?

solution.explanation: Complaints can be filed online on the CMS portal (cms.rbi.org.in), by e-mail to crpc@rbi.org.in, or physically with the Centralised Receipt and Processing Centre (CRPC) in Chandigarh.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other addresses are not the designated complaint e-mail under the Scheme.

fact_checks.claim: Procedure for filing a complaint: online through the CMS portal at https://cms.rbi.org.in; e-mail by sending the complaint to crpc@rbi.org.in; physical mode to the Centralised Receipt and Processing Centre, Chandigarh

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Assuming all procedural conditions are met, which of the following grievances can be maintained before the RBI Ombudsman under RB-IOS, 2026?

options.text: A customer's complaint that her bank did not credit interest on her deposit as per its terms
A customer's grievance against the bank's managing director personally
An employee's grievance about salary arrears from the bank that employs him
A software vendor's dispute with a bank over payment of its invoices

solution.explanation: The Scheme covers deficiency in service by a covered Regulated Entity to its customer. Disputes between a vendor and an RE, employer-employee disputes, and grievances against the management or executives of an RE are listed as non-maintainable.
steps: Deposit interest not credited → deficiency in service → maintainable
Vendor dispute, employment dispute, grievance against executives → non-maintainable
solution.why_others_wrong: The other three are expressly excluded categories.
solution.final_answer: Option A: A customer's complaint that her bank did not credit interest on her deposit as per its terms

fact_checks.claim: Not maintainable: disputes between a vendor and a Regulated Entity; grievances against Management or Executives of a Regulated Entity; disputes involving employee-employer relationship of a Regulated Entity

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: An appeal is filed before the Appellate Authority against an Award of the RBI Ombudsman under RB-IOS, 2026. Which of the following can the Appellate Authority do?

options.text: Impose a penalty on the complainant for filing the complaint
Transfer the case to the Banking Ombudsman of another State
Remand the matter to the RBI Ombudsman for fresh disposal with directions
Refer the complaint to a civil court for trial

solution.explanation: The Appellate Authority may allow the appeal and set aside the Award, remand the matter to the RBI Ombudsman for fresh disposal with directions, modify the Award and pass directions to give effect to it, or pass any other order it deems fit.
steps: Options: set aside / remand / modify / other order
solution.why_others_wrong: Referral to a civil court and penalising the complainant are not provided; under 'One Nation One Ombudsman' there is no State-wise transfer.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Remand the matter to the RBI Ombudsman for fresh disposal with directions

fact_checks.claim: The Appellate Authority may allow the appeal and set aside the Award; remand the matter to the RBI Ombudsman for fresh disposal with appropriate directions; modify the Award and pass directions; or pass any other order as it may deem fit

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Ravi's bank froze his savings account in compliance with a written order of a law enforcement agency. He complains to the RBI Ombudsman about the freeze. Under RB-IOS, 2026, his complaint is:

options.text: Maintainable, since freezing an account is a deficiency in service
To be transferred by the Ombudsman to the police for decision
Maintainable only if the freeze lasted more than 30 days
Not maintainable, as the bank acted in compliance with an order of a law enforcement authority

solution.explanation: Grievances arising from action taken by a Regulated Entity in compliance with orders of a judicial, quasi-judicial, statutory or law enforcing authority are not maintainable under the Scheme.
steps: Action taken on a law enforcement order → excluded ground
solution.why_others_wrong: Such compliance is not a deficiency in service; there is no 30-day condition; the Ombudsman does not transfer complaints to the police.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Not maintainable, as the bank acted in compliance with an order of a law enforcement authority

fact_checks.claim: Not maintainable: grievances arising from action taken by a Regulated Entity in compliance with orders of a judicial/quasi-judicial, statutory or law enforcing authority

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about RB-IOS, 2026:
I. The Appellate Authority can only confirm or set aside an Award; it cannot modify it.
II. A Regulated Entity may appeal (with the required prior approval) within 30 days of receiving the complainant's letter accepting the Award, and the Appellate Authority may allow up to 30 more days for sufficient reason.
III. A complainant may voluntarily withdraw a complaint at any stage, through the 'Track a complaint' tab on the CMS portal.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The Appellate Authority can also remand or modify an Award (I wrong). An RE's appeal lies within 30 days of receipt of the complainant's acceptance letter, extendable by up to 30 days (II correct). A complaint may be withdrawn at any stage via 'Track a complaint' on CMS (III correct).
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with I are wrong; 'III only' misses II.
solution.final_answer: Option D: II and III only

fact_checks.claim: A Regulated Entity may also file an appeal within 30 days from the date of receipt of the complainant's letter accepting the Award, subject to the required prior approval; the Appellate Authority may allow a further period of up to 30 days; the Appellate Authority may modify the Award
A complainant may voluntarily withdraw a complaint at any stage by logging on to the CMS portal and going to the tab 'Track a complaint'

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Asha wants to buy a ₹15 item but has only a ₹20 denomination in her retail e₹ wallet. According to RBI's e₹ FAQs, what happens?

options.text: The merchant must return ₹5 in cash
She must first load a ₹10 and a ₹5 denomination from her bank account
She enters ₹15; the merchant gets ₹15 and ₹5 stays in her wallet
She must pay ₹20 and the merchant credits ₹5 as a voucher

solution.concept: Change feature of the e₹ wallet
solution.explanation: e₹ is held in denominations like cash, but every e₹ wallet has a change feature: the user enters the amount; ₹15 is credited to the merchant automatically and the balance ₹5 remains in the wallet.
solution.why_others_wrong: No extra loading, cash change or voucher is needed.
solution.final_answer: Option C: She enters ₹15; the merchant gets ₹15 and ₹5 stays in her wallet

fact_checks.claim: If one desires to purchase a ₹15 item but has only ₹20 denomination in the e₹ wallet, she can enter ₹15 in the amount field; ₹15 will automatically be credited to the merchant while the balance ₹5 will remain in the e₹ wallet

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under the RBI (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025, when a recovery agent is assigned to a defaulted digital loan (or the agent is changed), what must the lender do?

options.text: Inform the borrower only after the dues are recovered
Publish the agent's name in a national newspaper
Obtain the borrower's written consent to the appointment
Send the agent's particulars to the borrower by e-mail/SMS before the agent contacts the borrower

solution.explanation: The Directions require that the particulars of the recovery agent authorised to approach the borrower be communicated to the borrower through e-mail/SMS before the agent contacts the borrower.
steps: Particulars to borrower by e-mail/SMS first
solution.why_others_wrong: No newspaper notice or borrower consent is prescribed; telling the borrower afterwards defeats the purpose.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Send the agent's particulars to the borrower by e-mail/SMS before the agent contacts the borrower

fact_checks.claim: In case of a loan default, when a recovery agent is assigned for recovery or there is a change in the recovery agent, the particulars of such recovery agent shall be communicated to the borrower through email/ SMS before the recovery agent contacts the borrower for recovery

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Card tokenisation replaces actual card details with a unique 'token' for payments through phones, wearables and other devices. According to RBI, who can perform tokenisation and de-tokenisation?

options.text: The authorised card network or the card issuer
The token requestor app on the customer's device

solution.explanation: RBI's FAQs say tokenisation and de-tokenisation can be performed by the authorised card network or by the card issuer (the token service provider). Token requestors cannot store the card number; the merchant never receives actual card details. The service is free and optional for customers.
steps: Token service provider = card network or card issuer
solution.why_others_wrong: Merchants and token requestors cannot hold card details; NIC has no role.
solution.final_answer: Option A: The authorised card network or the card issuer

fact_checks.claim: Tokenisation and de-tokenisation can be performed by the authorised card network or by the card issuer; token requestor cannot store Primary Account Number (PAN) or any other card detail

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under the RBI (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025, in which of the following forms can a regulated entity NOT accept a default loss guarantee (DLG) from a lending service provider?

options.text: Cash deposited with the regulated entity
A corporate guarantee issued by the LSP's parent company
A fixed deposit with a scheduled commercial bank, with lien marked in favour of the regulated entity
A bank guarantee in favour of the regulated entity

solution.explanation: A regulated entity may accept DLG only as cash deposited with it, a fixed deposit with a scheduled commercial bank with lien marked in its favour, or a bank guarantee in its favour.
steps: Permitted: cash, lien-marked FD with an SCB, bank guarantee
solution.why_others_wrong: The other three are exactly the permitted forms.
solution.final_answer: Option B: A corporate guarantee issued by the LSP's parent company

fact_checks.claim: RE shall accept DLG only in one or more of the following forms: cash deposited with the RE; fixed deposit maintained with a Scheduled Commercial Bank with a lien marked in favour of the RE; bank guarantee in favour of the RE

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Retail e₹ wallets are normally linked to the user's savings bank account. According to RBI's e₹ FAQs, how can beneficiaries of a Direct Benefit Transfer scheme receiving benefits through programmable CBDC be on-boarded?

options.text: Only through a savings account opened under PMJDY
Only by visiting an RBI regional office with KYC documents
Through a credit card issued by a public sector bank
Through mobile and/or Aadhaar number authentication, without a savings account being mandatory

solution.explanation: RBI notes that for programmable CBDC use cases such as DBT, the on-boarding criteria were modified: such users can on-board on the CBDC app through mobile and/or Aadhaar number authentication, and a savings account is not mandatory for them.
steps: General e₹ wallets → linked to savings account
DBT via programmable CBDC → mobile/Aadhaar authentication
solution.why_others_wrong: A PMJDY account, an RBI office visit or a credit card are not the prescribed route.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Through mobile and/or Aadhaar number authentication, without a savings account being mandatory

fact_checks.claim: For eligible beneficiaries of a Direct Benefit Transfer scheme receiving government benefits through Programmable CBDC, the on-boarding criteria has been modified; such users can get themselves on-boarded on CBDC App through Mobile and / or Aadhaar Number authentication; for such users it is not mandatory to have a savings account

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about default loss guarantee (DLG) arrangements under the RBI (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025:
I. The regulated entity must invoke the DLG within a maximum overdue period of 120 days, unless the borrower makes good the dues earlier.
II. Once the DLG is invoked, the amount is set off against the borrower's loan, reducing what the borrower owes.
III. Where the DLG provider is itself a regulated entity, it must deduct the full outstanding DLG amount from its capital.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: DLG must be invoked within a maximum overdue period of 120 days (I correct). The invoked amount is not set off against individual loans: the borrower's liability is unaffected (II wrong). An RE acting as DLG provider deducts the full outstanding DLG from its capital (III correct). Once invoked, DLG cannot be reinstated.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options containing II are wrong; 'I only' omits III.
solution.final_answer: Option C: I and III only

fact_checks.claim: RE shall invoke DLG within a maximum overdue period of 120 days, unless the loan dues are made good by the borrower before that

The amount of DLG invoked shall not be set off against the underlying individual loans, i.e. the liability of the borrowers shall remain unaffected; in case DLG provider is an RE, it shall deduct full amount of the DLG which is outstanding from its capital

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's payments booklet (January 2021), UPI transactions use two-factor authentication through device binding and a UPI PIN. Which technology is used to encrypt the UPI PIN?

solution.explanation: RBI's payments booklet notes that the UPI PIN is encrypted using Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), while transaction data is stored in encrypted form in the app provider's system.
solution.why_others_wrong: RFID is used in FASTag, NFC in contactless cards and MICR in cheques.

fact_checks.claim: Transactions are carried out through mobile devices with two factor authentication using device binding and a UPI PIN; the UPI PIN is encrypted using Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) technology

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under the UPI–PayNow linkage between India and Singapore, what is the daily limit for cross-border remittances?

solution.explanation: RBI's FAQs on the UPI–PayNow linkage state a daily transaction limit of ₹60,000 (around SGD 1,000) for cross-border remittances.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other amounts are not the prescribed limit.

fact_checks.claim: There is a daily transaction limit of ₹60,000 in a day (equivalent to around SGD 1,000) for undertaking cross-border remittance transactions through the UPI-PayNow linkage

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: What makes payments using a UPI Virtual Payment Address (VPA) more secure, according to RBI's payments booklet (January 2021)?

options.text: VPA payments are settled in RBI's books in real time
A VPA can be created only at a bank branch
The payer does not need the beneficiary's account or bank details
Each VPA is valid for only one transaction

solution.explanation: RBI notes that the unique feature of VPA-based transactions is their security: they obviate the need for sharing account or bank details with the remitter. Users set their own VPA. Transfers can also be made using account number and IFSC.
steps: No sharing of account details → secure
solution.why_others_wrong: VPAs are reusable; UPI settles on a deferred net basis; VPAs are created in apps, not at branches.
solution.final_answer: Option C: The payer does not need the beneficiary's account or bank details

fact_checks.claim: UPI users send and receive money using a Virtual Payment Address (VPA) set by the user; the unique feature of VPA based transaction is the secure aspect of UPI architecture as it obviates the need for sharing account or bank details

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Third-party application providers (TPAPs) such as Google Pay and WhatsApp offer UPI payments. As described in RBI's payments booklet (January 2021), which statement about them is correct?

options.text: TPAPs connect directly to the UPI switch and bear full liability for their transactions
Only banks can connect directly to the UPI switch; TPAPs partner with a bank, which bears the operational and financial liability
TPAPs settle UPI transactions through their own accounts with RBI
TPAPs are licensed by RBI as payment banks before joining UPI

solution.explanation: The UPI ecosystem is designed for banks: only a banking entity can directly interact with the UPI switch. Non-banks participate by partnering with a bank already on UPI. The entire operational and financial liability for transactions through the third-party app lies on the bank.
solution.why_others_wrong: TPAPs do not connect directly, are not licensed as payments banks for this, and do not settle with RBI.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Only banks can connect directly to the UPI switch; TPAPs partner with a bank, which bears the operational and financial liability

fact_checks.claim: Only a banking entity can directly interact with the UPI switch; non-banking entities can participate by partnering with a banking entity already on the UPI platform; the entire operational and financial liability of transactions originated through third party app lies on the bank

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the UPI–PayNow linkage, based on RBI's FAQs:
I. Only person-to-person remittances for 'Maintenance of Relatives Abroad' and 'Gift' are allowed, within the Liberalised Remittance Scheme limits.
II. Apps of participating Indian banks offer an opt-in/opt-out feature for receiving remittances from Singapore.
III. A remittance from Singapore can be received in an Indian bank account using a UPI ID registered with a different bank.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: Only P2P remittances for maintenance of relatives abroad and gift are permitted, subject to LRS limits (I correct). There is an opt-in/opt-out feature for inward remittances (II correct). Presently, only a UPI ID registered with the same bank where the account is held can be used (III wrong).
steps: III ✗ (UPI ID must be with the same bank)
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with III are wrong; 'I only' misses II.
solution.final_answer: Option D: I and II only

Presently, the UPI ID registered with the same bank where account is held can only be used

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: UPI handled 25.47 billion transactions worth ₹31.53 lakh crore in October 2026, against 24.07 billion worth ₹29.37 lakh crore in September 2026. The average daily value rose from ₹97,913 crore to ₹1,01,707 crore. Why did the average daily value rise by only about 3.9% when the monthly value rose by about 7.4%?

options.text: The monthly value includes UPI Lite payments, which the daily average excludes
Daily averages count only working days, and October had more holidays
The number of transactions fell in October, which held down the daily average
October has 31 days against September's 30, so part of the monthly rise comes from the extra day

solution.explanation: Monthly value rose 7.4% (29.37 → 31.53). Daily averages are monthly value ÷ days: 31.53 lakh crore ÷ 31 ≈ ₹1,01,700 crore and 29.37 lakh crore ÷ 30 ≈ ₹97,900 crore, a rise of about 3.9%. The gap is the day-count effect: 1.039 × 31/30 ≈ 1.074.
steps: 1.039 × (31 ÷ 30) ≈ 1.074 → the difference is the extra day
solution.shortcut: Growth in totals ≈ growth in daily average + growth in number of days (3.9% + 3.3% ≈ 7.4%).
solution.why_others_wrong: Volume rose (24.07 → 25.47 billion); the daily figures match value ÷ calendar days, so no working-day or UPI Lite adjustment is involved.
solution.final_answer: Option D: October has 31 days against September's 30, so part of the monthly rise comes from the extra day

fact_checks.claim: UPI recorded 25.47 billion transactions worth Rs 31.53 lakh crore in October; average daily transaction value increased to Rs 1,01,707 crore from Rs 97,913 crore in the previous month; in September 2026, UPI recorded 24.07 billion transactions worth Rs 29.37 lakh crore (published 2 November 2026)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness

solution.explanation: NEFT is a net-settlement system with 48 batches in 24 hours; the first batch is at 0030 hours and the last at midnight.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other pairs either do not span 48 half-hour batches or start at the wrong time.

fact_checks.claim: NEFT settlement works on net-settlement in batches, with 48 batches of settlement over a span of 24 hours, the first and last batches taking place at 0030 hours and midnight, respectively

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness

options.text: It settles some transactions gross and some net
It has features of both retail and large-value systems, with no floor or ceiling on amounts
It is operated jointly by RBI and NPCI
It accepts both paper and electronic instructions for settlement

solution.explanation: RBI's booklet says NEFT is a unique hybrid payment system because it carries characteristics of both a retail and a large-value payment system, offering round-the-clock transfers with no floor or ceiling on amounts. Its average transaction value is about ₹10 lakh.
solution.why_others_wrong: NEFT settles only on a net batch basis, is owned and operated by RBI alone, and is an electronic system.
solution.final_answer: Option B: It has features of both retail and large-value systems, with no floor or ceiling on amounts

fact_checks.claim: NEFT is a unique hybrid payment system as it carries with it the characteristics of both a retail and a large value payment system, offering round the clock transfers with no floor or ceiling on the amounts; average transaction value of approximately ten lakh rupees

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under the Indo-Nepal Remittance Facility Scheme, which uses NEFT, how does money sent from India reach the beneficiary in Nepal?

options.text: It is paid out in Indian rupees by Indian post offices in Nepal
It flows to a designated SBI branch, which transfers it to Nepal SBI Bank Ltd for disbursal in Nepalese currency
It is credited by RBI directly to the Nepal Rastra Bank
It is routed through NPCI's IMPS to any bank in Nepal

The money flows to a designated SBI branch, which consolidates and transfers it to Nepal SBI Bank Ltd (NSBL); NSBL disburses it in local currency, through banks or banks plus money transfer agents.
steps: NEFT → designated SBI branch → Nepal SBI Bank Ltd → beneficiary (Nepalese rupees)
solution.why_others_wrong: IMPS, Nepal Rastra Bank and post offices are not part of the channel.
solution.final_answer: Option B: It flows to a designated SBI branch, which transfers it to Nepal SBI Bank Ltd for disbursal in Nepalese currency

fact_checks.claim: The money flows to a designated branch of SBI, which consolidates and transfers the amount to Nepal SBI Bank Ltd. (NSBL); NSBL disburses the remittance to beneficiaries in Nepal in the local currency

In Nepal, the INRF Scheme is handled by Nepal SBI Ltd. (NSBL) ... the remittance information is conveyed electronically by SBI in a secure mode to NSBL. NSBL then makes arrangements for credit to the bank account of the beneficiary ... Else, NSBL disburses funds in cash

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's current FAQs on the Indo-Nepal Remittance Facility (INRF) Scheme, Ram, who has an account with an NEFT-enabled branch, wants to send ₹9 lakh to his family in Nepal during a year, and Shyam, a walk-in customer with no account, wants to send ₹7.5 lakh in the year. What is the position?

options.text: Both are capped at 12 remittances of ₹50,000, so each can send at most ₹6 lakh
Ram can send the full ₹9 lakh, in at least 5 remittances; Shyam can send at most ₹6 lakh
Ram needs at least 18 remittances; Shyam can send the full ₹7.5 lakh in 15 remittances
Ram can send at most ₹2 lakh in the year; Shyam can send at most ₹6 lakh

solution.concept: INRF limits for account holders and walk-in customers
solution.explanation: A sender with an account at an NEFT-enabled branch can remit up to ₹2 lakh per transaction with no limit on the number of remittances, so Ram needs at least 9 ÷ 2 rounded up = 5 remittances. A walk-in customer can remit up to ₹50,000 per remittance and at most 12 remittances a year, a ceiling of ₹6 lakh, so ₹1.5 lakh of Shyam's amount cannot go through the scheme that year.
steps: Account holder: ₹2 lakh per transaction, no cap on number → 9 ÷ 2 → 5 remittances
Walk-in: 12 × ₹50,000 = ₹6 lakh a year → ₹1.5 lakh left over
solution.why_others_wrong: The ₹50,000 × 12 cap applies only to walk-in customers; ₹2 lakh is a per-transaction limit, not an annual one; 18 remittances assumes the walk-in limit for Ram, and 15 remittances exceed Shyam's cap of 12.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Ram can send the full ₹9 lakh, in at least 5 remittances; Shyam can send at most ₹6 lakh

fact_checks.claim: One can remit upto ₹2 lakhs per transaction to the beneficiary residing in Nepal; provided the sender maintains account with any NEFT enabled bank branch in India. Walk-in / Non-customer can remit upto ₹50,000 per transaction ... There is no limit on remittances if the sender is maintaining account with any NEFT enabled bank-branch in India. Walk-in / Non-customers are allowed to remit 12 remittances in a year with ceiling of ₹50,000 per remittance

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements based on RBI's NEFT FAQs and payments booklet:
I. An optional field (tag 7495) in the NEFT message carries additional sender-to-receiver information, which destination banks should store and give the customer on request.
II. If a NEFT transaction is returned, the originating bank must show 'NEFT-Return' in the remitter's passbook or statement.
III. NEFT transactions are settled one by one on a gross basis in RBI's books.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: Tag 7495 is an optional field for sender-to-receiver information that destination banks should capture and provide on request (I correct). Returned transactions are shown as 'NEFT-Return' to the originator (II correct). NEFT settles on a net basis in half-hourly batches; gross settlement is RTGS (III wrong).
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with III are wrong; 'II only' misses I.
solution.final_answer: Option A: I and II only

NEFT settlement works on net-settlement in batches, with 48 batches of settlement over 24 hours

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the intraday liquidity (IDL) facility that RBI gave RTGS members, as described in RBI's payments booklet (January 2021):
I. IDL carries interest at the Bank Rate for the hours it is used.
II. IDL is extended against fully collateralised Indian government securities held in the member's IDL-SGL account.
III. IDL availed is reversed automatically by the RTGS system when the member's settlement account has sufficient funds above a threshold.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: IDL is extended free of interest (I wrong) against fully collateralised government securities in the IDL-SGL account (II correct). It is invoked automatically when funds are short and reversed automatically once sufficient funds are available (III correct). IDL not reversed by end of day attracts penal interest.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with I are wrong; 'III only' misses II.
solution.final_answer: Option D: II and III only

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's payments booklet (January 2021), at what point does NPCI route an IMPS transaction to the beneficiary bank?

options.text: Only after RBI has settled the transaction gross
Only after the beneficiary accepts the payment request
Before the remitter's account is debited, to save time
Only after the remitting bank has debited the remitter's account

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
